items.how: End the readiness check with a result or an error inside a bounded time, and re-enable 'Check if ready' when it ends so the reader can retry.
items.why: o1.png and s1.png both show the status stuck on 'Checking...' with the 'Check if ready' button disabled, so the reader never learns if the book is ready and the story fails.

s3.png shows the reader is told 'Ready at the front desk' with a hold deadline, and o-collect.png shows collecting is a 'Collect (staff only)' action at the desk, so a reader is not meant to collect in the app.

sides.position: A reader has no way to collect the book from the reservation page, so the story has no entry point.
sides.why: The reader view sends the reader to the front desk, and the staff view holds the collect action. Nothing is missing for the reader to act on.

sides.position: Signed in as desk staff, collect works.
sides.why: o-collect.png shows the collect action where the design puts it.

items.how: Keep the Reserve button visible at 1366x768 without scrolling: shorten the form, or pin the action bar under the fields.
items.why: o2.png and s2.png show the five-field form filling the 1366x768 window with no Reserve button in view, so a first-time reader may not find how to finish, even though the story completes.

items.how: Use one label for the action everywhere: 'Reserve a copy', which matches the story card, in place of 'Hold a book'.
items.why: o3.png shows 'Hold a book' on the reservation list while another page uses 'Reserve a copy', so a reader may think these are two different actions.
s4.png shows a fully loaded page and, in its own words, carries no timings, so a load of about ten seconds is not shown; deciding whether to measure load time belongs to the Captain.

deferred.how: Fix it together with i4: the shared label becomes 'Reserve a copy'.
deferred.why: No screenshot shows the long label itself. Reviewer o says it blocks them and s agrees with deferring it. Fixing it with i4's label change costs nothing extra and settles the disagreement.

The decline names host component Button at x.d.ts but does not name the missing prop, and no x.d.ts exists in the task world to check. With no declaration to read, I cannot uphold it, so the Captain decides whether to accept a departure from the host's look (kind host-look, owner Captain).

tasks.title: Make the readiness check finish and allow retry
tasks.scope: The check-ready status always ends in ready, not ready, or an error within a bounded time, and the 'Check if ready' button is re-enabled when it ends.

tasks.title: Keep Reserve in view and use one action label
tasks.scope: Show the Reserve button without scrolling at 1366x768, and use 'Reserve a copy' for the action on every page.
